name: simplify
description: Analyze source code complexity and get AI fix instructions for the most complex files. This tool runs ahma simplify to identify files with high cognitive/cyclomatic complexity, low maintainability, or excessive size, then returns a detailed report with per-function hotspots and actionable refactoring instructions. Always pass ai_fix set to the issue number you want to fix (1 = most complex file). The report identifies specific hotspot functions within each file. The structured prompt instructs you to focus changes on those hotspots only.

subcommand.name: default
subcommand.description: Run code simplicity analysis and return fix instructions for the Nth most complex file. Set ai_fix to the issue number (1 = worst file).

positional_args.name: directory
positional_args.description: Directory to analyze (absolute or relative path to the project root)

options.name: ai-fix
options.description: Issue number to generate AI fix instructions for (1 = most complex file, 2 = second most complex, etc.). When set, outputs the full report plus a structured prompt to simplify that file.

options.name: auto
options.description: Run all analysis lenses, prioritize findings across all lenses, and output prioritized fix actions for the top N most valuable items (default: 10). Example: ahma simplify --auto 6

options.name: limit
options.description: Number of top complexity issues to include in the report (default: 50)

options.name: html
options.description: Additionally render CODE_SIMPLICITY.html next to the Markdown report. Also causes the report to be written to disk rather than returned on stdout, so pair it with output_path when you want to know where it landed.

options.name: lens
options.description: Which analysis lenses to run. 'complexity' ranks files by cognitive/cyclomatic complexity and maintainability; 'reuse' detects duplicated code blocks across the project. Defaults to all lenses. Selecting only 'reuse' skips the complexity parse entirely and is much faster. Reuse findings are candidates for extraction, not defects — evaluate each one before acting.

options.name: diff
options.description: Analyze only files git reports as changed (staged, unstaged, and untracked) instead of the whole project. Use this to check work you just did rather than re-scanning everything. Fails if the directory is not a git repository.

options.name: extensions
options.description: File extensions or language names to analyze, comma-separated. Language names are case-insensitive and expand to all their extensions (e.g. 'rust' → rs, 'kotlin' → kt,kts). Supported languages: rust, python, javascript, typescript, kotlin, c, c++, java, c#, go, html, css. Raw extensions also work: rs, py, js, ts, tsx, kt, kts, c, h, cpp, cc, hpp, hh, cs, java, go, css, html. Default: all supported extensions

options.name: verify
options.description: Re-analyze a specific file and compare against the previous analysis baseline. Shows before/after metrics with relative improvement percentages. Requires a prior full analysis run.

options.name: output-path
options.description: Output directory for report files (CODE_SIMPLICITY.md/.html). If omitted, report is printed to stdout which is returned in the tool response.

install_instructions: Build with: cargo build -p ahma_mcp --release && cargo install --path ahma_mcp
